summary.oneLiner: Three-decade RF/microwave house re-rating itself from "Tier-2 subsystem supplier" to a Tier-1, IP-driven systems manufacturer and a DCPP (development-cum-production-partner) for strategic national programs. FY26 delivered turnover INR1,157cr (per guidance), 33%+ EBITDA margin, and a dramatic working-capital turnaround (OCF +INR370cr vs −INR99cr). Standalone order book INR2,141cr (consolidated ~INR2,600cr) + ~INR1,600cr+ bookable in FY27. Mgmt aspires to ~triple turnover in ~4.5–5.5 yrs (by ~FY30–31) on just 5–6 programs (QRSAM, Uttam, Su-30 Virupaksha radar, Su-30 Angad EW pod, ARC/JV, electronic mines) — explicitly excluding exports, BEL programs and future Astra-owned-IP/branded products (multiple to launch "before Diwali"). In-principle board approval to demerge Space/Meteorology/Hydrology business.
summary.business: The company designs, develops and manufactures RF and microwave systems, sub-systems and components, together with navigational, meteorological, geophysical and related instruments. Its product portfolio is stated to be exclusively electronics designed for Defence and Space applications, with no offerings directed toward the general consumer market. Customers are concentrated in strategic sectors - government agencies, defence public sector undertakings (DPSUs), public sector enterprises and other institutional clients - served from a domestic footprint of seven plants and two offices across 15 Indian states, with exports contributing 14% of turnover across two countries.

currentContext.strengths: Exclusive focus on defence and space electronics with no consumer exposure - the AR states the product portfolio is comprised solely of electronics for Defence and Space applications.|Entrenched position with strategic-sector buyers: key customers are government agencies, DPSUs, public sector enterprises and institutional clients, a customer set with high qualification and switching barriers.|Long operating history in a design-led business - incorporated 13-09-1991 and presenting its 35th Annual Report, covering design, development and manufacturing rather than assembly alone.|Reaffirmed credit standing: CRISIL A/Positive on long-term bank facilities and corporate credit rating, and CRISIL A1 on short-term bank facilities.|Skilled engineering base of 1,684 permanent employees (1,880 including non-permanent) with no worker cadre, consistent with a design and systems-integration model.|Assured non-financial reporting - BRSR Core disclosures carried Reasonable Assurance from Intertek India Private Limited.
currentContext.strategies: Reduce the environmental footprint through renewable self-generation - solar photovoltaic systems have been installed across offices and manufacturing facilities with a cumulative installed capacity of nearly 1 MW, described as supporting a transition towards cleaner energy and reduced reliance on fossil-fuel-based electricity.|Operate manufacturing effluent handling on Zero Liquid Discharge principles, with complete recycling and reuse of wastewater, treated sludge used for landscaping and gardening, and continuous monitoring to prevent any liquid discharge outside the premises.|Manage waste through a documented framework across all manufacturing facilities and offices, routing e-waste and hazardous waste exclusively through certified and licensed vendors, with landfilling and incineration reported at nil.|Pursue continuous facility-level resource-efficiency and safety projects - STP water pipelines to garden areas, solar water heaters in the canteen, gas bank centralisation, earth-pit renovation and ventilation upgrades - rather than a single large sustainability programme.|Contribute to afforestation and biodiversity through participation in programmes such as Telangana Haritha Haram, and reduce commuting emissions by providing shared transportation for employees.
currentContext.expansion: The routed capex_expansion sections carry no capacity, commissioning, ramp-up, debottlenecking or project narrative. The Management Discussion and Analysis extract routed here is in fact Directors'-Report boilerplate (dividend policy link, transfer to reserves, credit rating, stock-exchange listing, subsidiary/associate statement, board meeting count, Directors' Responsibility Statement) and contains no expansion content. The only structural changes disclosed are corporate-entity events rather than physical expansion: Astra Foundation was converted into Astra Private Limited on 12 March 2025 and struck off from the Register of Companies on 16 September 2025, and Bhavyabhanu Electronics Private Limited was renamed Astra Defence Technologies Private Limited on 18 November 2025 following a change in the company's main objects. The Chairman/MD extract routed here is BRSR Principle 1 and Principle 2 material, whose only capex-related statement is the leadership indicator that R&D and capital expenditure investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts were 0% of total R&D and 0% of total capex in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.

risks.risk: Data privacy and cyber security exposure in RF/microwave and digital electronics products
risks.note: The only material issue the BRSR table classifies as a Risk with NEGATIVE financial implications. The company states that in RF/Microwave/Digital electronics, hardware products and associated software can harbor security gaps that may threaten consumer data security, and that a failure to devise a comprehensive methodology to detect such vulnerabilities would place customer data at risk and undermine the customer relationship. Mitigation is a Cyber Risk Management framework overseen by the Information Technology & Security Committee and the Risk Management Committee, with controlled data access, encryption and stakeholder education. Structurally acute given a defence and space customer base.

The second material issue classified as a Risk in the BRSR table, with the company noting it is assessed on key governance areas such as ownership structure, board remuneration and accounting practices. The bundle text is truncated mid-row, so the stated mitigation and financial implication for this row are not readable. Board composition changes support the concern being live: two independent directors ceased during FY26 (22 May 2025 and 26 June 2025), two joined on 22 May 2025, and the CFO position turned over three times inside the year.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety hazards across manufacturing units
risks.note: The company runs a formal OHS management system across its units and Head Office covering routine and non-routine activities, with hazards scored on Likelihood x Severity, classes of Unacceptable or Needs Correction (L x S of 5 to 25) prioritised for corrective action, a designated Emergency Response Team, and 100% of plants and offices assessed for health and safety practices and working conditions. Reported outcomes for FY 2025-26 are nil across LTIFR, total recordable work-related injuries, fatalities and high-consequence injuries, so the risk is managed rather than currently crystallised.

risks.risk: Product design and technology obsolescence in RF and microwave technology
risks.note: Listed as material issue 1 and framed by the company as an OPPORTUNITY with positive implications, not a risk, but structurally it is a technology-cycle exposure: the company itself notes that competitive advantage, customer loyalty and market growth depend on staying at the forefront of technological advancements in RF and microwave technology. No mitigation approach is stated because the row is classified as an opportunity.

Listed as material issue 2 and framed as an opportunity with positive implications. For a design-and-development-led defence electronics business with no worker cadre, retention of engineering staff is a structural dependency; the company cites work-life balance, career development, competitive compensation and work environment as the levers that drive morale, productivity and retention. No complaints on working conditions or health and safety were filed in FY 2025-26 or FY 2024-25.

risks.risk: Supply chain sustainability and supplier dependence
risks.note: Listed as material issue 3, again framed as an opportunity. The company notes that firms actively managing supply-chain impacts through standards, monitoring and supplier engagement may be better positioned to protect shareholder value in the long run, implying that unmanaged supplier exposure is the corresponding downside. No mitigation approach is stated because the row is classified as an opportunity.

risks.risk: Energy management and clean technology transition
risks.note: Listed as material issue 4 and classified as an opportunity with positive implications: the company links reduced energy consumption and integration of renewable energy sources to lower operational costs and carbon footprint, and ties clean technology to reputation and market position. The residual exposure is energy cost and the pace of the transition rather than a flagged risk.

- Margins: mgmt flagged ~33%/55% as likely the top end — model "slightly lower" to avoid disappointment; aims to sustain rather than expand.
- ~$0.5bn+ revenue enterprise "in the immediate coming decade," potentially much larger.
order book & pipeline:
- Standalone order book INR2,141cr (consolidated ~INR2,600cr) as on Mar 31, 2026.
- Q4 fresh orders ~INR530cr; PNC concluded on ~INR300cr more (expected in next couple of months).
- Key Q4 wins: SDR programs; radar subsystems from BEL; Gaganyaan checkout hardware (ISRO).
- FY27 bookable pipeline ~INR1,600cr+.
- Total addressable opportunity ~INR28,000cr (FY26–FY28 deck) — quantum unchanged but timeline slipped (govt-program delays) from ~FY28–29 toward ~FY30–31.
- Near-term order catalysts: Uttam AESA (HAL negotiations near final, order expected Q2/Q3); QRSAM (awaiting BEL prime contract ~June; FOPM small-qty orders already flowing); BEL programs (Nayan Shakti, Hima Shakti, Shatrughna).
segment:
- Radar (~60% FY26 rev): ground/airborne, fire-control, surveillance & tracking, short/medium/long-range; AAAU for Virupaksha (Super Sukhoi); futuristic digital-array radar (delivered to DRDO), photonics/optical radar (with startup), counter-drone "Drishti/D4," GPR (with startup), bird-detection, miniaturised radars. Delivered complete systems to SHAR/ISRO, ITR/DRDO, PXE.
- EW & missiles (~part of 25%): Su-30 Angad pod jammer (DCPP, one of two selected); active seekers for couple of missiles; electronic mines flagged as a big area.
- Space & meteorology (~16% FY26): satellite earth stations; complete X/C/S-band Doppler weather radars (IMD); L/S/UHF wind-profiler radars; defence-satellite complex subsystems (constellation repeat orders expected). To be demerged.
- MMIC: in-house chip division (created 2005); supplies most active devices captively; now promoting MMICs to domestic & international players.
growth verticals: Drivers: indigenisation (~75% capital-acquisition budget domestic); airborne/fire-control/surveillance/long-range radars; EW airborne platforms (post-qualification production orders); missile active seekers; space repeat orders (ISRO + defence satellites); meteorology production orders (Doppler/wind-profiler) yet to come. Strategic up-the-value-chain shift: component → IP-driven systems → DCPP → Astra-owned-IP/branded products (multiple before Diwali, first NCNC demo this quarter) for India-first then global markets. Exports re-based on high-value-add/IP (via ARC with Rafael) rather than low-margin BTP/offset.
margins: FY26 gross ~55%, Q4 EBITDA ~33.3% — driven by favourable mix (space + higher-value exports). Space margins > defence but only ~10–15% of sales, so mix swings have limited overall impact. New export model (co-developed RF for Rafael SDRs) carries ~40–45% gross vs single-digit legacy BTP. Mgmt explicit: current level is roughly the top end; sustain rather than expand; model slightly lower to avoid disappointment.
capex: Steady-state ~INR40–50cr/yr augmentation; no large step-up needed to fund the 3x ambition — most capacity already in place. Growth funded mainly via working capital. Increased R&D spend YoY (product/solution development) expected to convert to medium/long-term business.
capital allocation: Dividend INR2.40/share (120% of FV) for FY26. Major working-capital improvement: OCF +INR370cr (vs −INR99cr) via realising long-held receivables; expects further improvement and to stay within sanctioned bank limits (finance cost roughly flat). Rising R&D investment. In-principle board approval to demerge Space/Meteorology/Hydrology business — detailed scheme expected within weeks — to sharpen focus, governance and create clearer shareholder investment propositions.
risks:
- Govt-driven program timing/delays (budget & priority) — TAM intact but slipping ~2 yrs (FY28–29 → FY30–31).
- Back-ended (rear-ended) 3x growth concentrated in 5–6 programs — execution & qualification gating (Su-30 radar qualify ~FY28, production possibly 2–3 yrs later; BEL flagged Su-30 still in development ~5 yrs).
- JV forex exposure (~$2m provision hit FY26 profit).
- Margin near top end — downside if mix shifts.
- Working-capital intensity rises with volume.
- Unproven proprietary-IP/branded products (timelines "before Diwali" / "by November") — execution-contingent upside, not yet de-risked.
mgmt tone: Confident, long-term, philosophy-heavy (Atim Kabra: "speak less, think long term, deliver"; "only the paranoid survive"). Strong "under-promise" framing — repeatedly told analysts to model lower margins and stressed 3x excludes exports/BEL/IP products ("gravy on top"). Proud re-rating narrative (Tier-1 systems house, DCPP, holy-grail Astra-branded IP) anchored in listed delivered systems. Candid on delays being government-side, not execution-side.
non-obvious:
- 3x turnover aspiration rests on just 5–6 programs (QRSAM, Uttam, Su-30 Virupaksha radar, Su-30 Angad EW pod, JV/ARC, electronic mines) — exports, BEL programs and Astra-owned-IP products are all EXCLUDED upside.
- "Virupaksha"/Uttam radar AAAU is a DRDO program where Astra develops the active antenna array unit; Uttam order to be placed by HAL (not DRDO directly).
- Su-30 EW pod ("Angad") — Astra is one of two selected DCPPs.
- Astra-owned, Astra-branded IP products (complete IP with Astra) to launch "before Diwali"; first NCNC demo this quarter — entirely outside guidance.
- Demerger of Space/Met/Hydrology in-principle approved — scheme in weeks; reshapes the ~16% space segment into a standalone vehicle.
- Photonics (optical-domain) radar and GPR developed with startup partners; digital-array radar subsystems already delivered to DRDO.
- MMIC: zero supply issues; pivoting from purely captive to also selling chips to domestic + international players.
- Export "exports" line is largely sales to own JV ARC (co-developed RF for Rafael SDRs), not third-party — high value-add.

segment:

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The company designs, develops and manufactures RF and microwave systems, sub-systems and components, together with navigational, meteorological, geophysical and related instruments. Its product portfolio is stated to be exclusively electronics designed for Defence and Space applications, with no offerings directed toward the general consumer market. Customers are concentrated in strategic sectors - government agencies, defence public sector undertakings (DPSUs), public sector enterprises and other institutional clients - served from a domestic footprint of seven plants and two offices across 15 Indian states, with exports contributing 14% of turnover across two countries.

- ARC/JV: FY26 orders INR546cr / sales INR360cr, share of profit ~INR8cr (forex-hit); FY27 ≥50% growth, sales >INR600cr, profit ≥INR20cr.
- New disclosures: in-principle demerger of Space/Met/Hydrology; Astra-owned-IP/branded products before Diwali (first NCNC demo this quarter); $0.5bn+ revenue aspiration; TAM ~INR28,000cr timeline pushed ~2 yrs; dividend INR2.40 (120% FV).

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] The Board has given in-principle approval to demerge the Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business undertakings into a separate entity, to enable focused management attention, tailored growth strategies and capital allocation, and unlocking of value; the final decision on structure and share exchange ratio is pending consultants' reports and opinions.
- [Demerger metrics - attribution unclear] The demerger slide carries Rs 110.6 Cr "FY26 Revenue", Rs 187.1 Cr "Orderbook As on March 2026" and Rs 154.0 Cr "Order guidance", but the deck does not state which entity or undertaking these figures belong to.
- [Leadership] Mr S. Gurunatha Reddy steps down as Managing Director with effect from 30 September 2026 and continues as Executive Director; Dr M. V. Reddy assumes the Managing Director role from 1 October 2026, subject to Board approval.
- [Market sizing] The deck cites major opportunities for AMPL of around Rs 24,000-25,000 Cr across all sectors till FY28, an Indian radar market of ~Rs 12,200 crores by 2033 at 20.62% CAGR, an Indian EW market of ~Rs 9,500 crores by 2033 at 4.47% CAGR, and an FY2026-27 budgeted defence budget of INR 7.7 lac cr (source cited: KPMG Report).
- [Q1FY27 orders] Major orders received in Q1 FY27 total Rs 172.6 Cr, led by Radar for BEL Bangalore Rs 93.6 Cr and Space for SAC Rs 49.3 Cr; the FY26 top-10 orders total Rs 657.0 Cr, led by Meteorology for IMD Rs 145.2 Cr and an ARC export order of Rs 138.0 Cr.
